data.gender_notes: Aishiki is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aishiki is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Aish' which means 'feelings' or 'emotions'. This name is used to evoke a sense of deep connection and emotional intelligence. It is believed that those named Aishiki are naturally attuned to their own feelings and those of others, making them compassionate and wise. The name Aishiki carries the meaning “Feelings, Emotions” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aishiki usually hope their child will grow to embody feelings, emotions and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Aishiki belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Feelings, Emotions.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aishiki total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

In Hindu philosophy, emotions are seen as a bridge between the physical and spiritual realms, allowing individuals to connect with various deities and experiences.

historical_references.reference: Aishiki was a renowned Hindu poetess from the 13th century, known for her devotional poetry in Bengali and Sanskrit languages. She was a prominent figure in the Bhakti movement and is considered one of the most influential women poets in Indian literary history.

Another reference suggests that Aishiki was a queen of the Sena Dynasty in Bengal during the 12th or 13th century. She is believed to have composed several songs in the Bengali language, expressing her deep devotion to the goddess Kali.
